summary: How many threads must a person weave on Shabbos to be chayav? Rabbi Eliezer says three at the start or one more on cloth, and the Sages say two either way.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer says: One who weaves on Shabbat is liable to bring a sin-offering if he wove

chunks.en: one who weaves three threads at the start,
chunks.st: three threads at the beginning of something new,

chunks.en: or one thread onto woven cloth,
chunks.st: or if he adds one thread to a preexisting woven fabric.

chunks.en: is chayav. And the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: whether at the beginning or at the end,
chunks.st: Both at the beginning and at the end,

chunks.en: its amount is two threads.
chunks.st: its measure for liability is two threads.

summary: Making two loops on a loom, a sifter, or a basket is a melacha. So is sewing two stitches, or tearing in order to sew two stitches.
stIntro: One who makes two meshes, i.e., ties the threads of the warp, attaching them

chunks.en: One who makes two loops on the loom heddles,
chunks.st: to either the nirin or

words.note: Parts of a loom that hold the threads.

chunks.en: on the reed, on a sifter,
chunks.st: the keiros, which will be explained in the Gemara, in a winnow,

chunks.en: on a sieve, or on a basket,
chunks.st: sieve, or basket,

chunks.en: is chayav. And one who sews two stitches,
chunks.st: is liable for making meshes. And one who sews is liable if he sews two stitches.

chunks.he: וְהַקּוֹרֵעַ עַל מְנָת לִתְפֹּר שְׁתֵּי תְפִירוֹת:
chunks.en: and one who tears in order to sew two stitches.
chunks.st: And one who tears is liable if he tears enough fabric in order to sew two stitches to repair it.

summary: Someone who only ruins things on Shabbos is patur, like tearing his clothes out of anger or for a relative who died. But ruining something in order to fix it counts like fixing.

chunks.en: One who tears his clothes in his anger or for his dead relative,
chunks.st: One who rends his garment in his anger or in anguish over his dead relative is exempt.

chunks.en: and anyone who only ruins things,
chunks.st: And anyone else who performs labors destructively on Shabbat

chunks.en: is patur. But one who ruins in order to fix,
chunks.st: is exempt. And one who performs a labor destructively in order to repair is liable, and

chunks.en: his amount is like one who fixes.
chunks.st: his measure for liability is equivalent to the measure for one who performs that labor constructively.

summary: This mishnah gives the amounts for whitening, combing, dyeing, spinning, and weaving that make a person chayav on Shabbos.

chunks.en: The amount for one who whitens, combs, dyes, or spins wool
chunks.st: for one who whitens, or one who combs, or one who dyes, or one who spins wool is

chunks.en: is the full width of a double sit.
chunks.st: the full width of a double sit,
chunks.stMore: which is the distance between the forefinger and the middle finger.

words.note: The space between the pointer finger and the middle finger.

chunks.en: And one who weaves two threads:
chunks.st: And for one who weaves two threads,

chunks.en: his amount is the full sit.
chunks.st: the measure that determines liability is one sit.

summary: Trapping an animal on Shabbos is a melacha only if it is really caught and cannot get away. The Rabbis argue about which places count as catching it.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: one who traps a bird into a cage, or a deer into a house,
chunks.st: One who traps a bird into a closet or cage, and one who traps a deer into a house

chunks.en: is chayav. And the Sages say,
chunks.st: is liable. The Rabbis say: One is liable for trapping

chunks.en: a bird into a cage,
chunks.st: a bird into a closet

chunks.en: and a deer into a house, a courtyard, or an animal pen.
chunks.st: and for trapping a deer into a garden, or into a courtyard, or into an enclosure [bivar], he is liable.

chunks.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says,
chunks.st: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

chunks.en: not all animal pens are the same.
chunks.st: Not all enclosures are identical.

chunks.en: This is the rule:
chunks.st: This is the principle: If the

chunks.en: if it still needs to be caught,
chunks.st: trapping of the animal is inadequate
chunks.stMore: and it is still necessary to pursue and apprehend it, one is

chunks.en: he is patur; if it does not still need to be caught, he is chayav.
chunks.st: not liable. However, if one trapped a deer into an enclosure in which the trapping is not inadequate, he is liable.

summary: If a deer walked into a house and one person locked the door, he is chayav for trapping. If two people locked it together, it depends on whether one person could have done it alone.

chunks.he: צְבִי שֶׁנִּכְנַס לַבַּיִת וְנָעַל אֶחָד בְּפָנָיו,
chunks.en: A deer that went into a house, and one person locked the door in front of it,
chunks.st: a deer entered a house on its own and one locked the door before it,

chunks.en: he is chayav. If two locked it,
chunks.st: he is liable for trapping. If two people locked the door,

chunks.he: פְּטוּרִין. לֹא יָכֹל אֶחָד לִנְעֹל וְנָעֲלוּ שְׁנַיִם,
chunks.en: they are patur. If one could not lock it and two locked it,
chunks.st: they are exempt, because neither performed a complete labor. If one person is incapable of locking the door and two people locked it,

chunks.en: they are chayav. But Rabbi Shimon says they are patur.
chunks.st: they are liable because that is the typical manner of performing that labor. And Rabbi Shimon deems them exempt
chunks.stMore: as he holds that two people who perform a single labor are never liable by Torah law.

summary: If two people sit in a doorway to trap a deer, the one who fully blocks the door is chayav. Someone who sits there after the deer is already trapped is like someone who locks his house with a deer already inside.

chunks.he: יָשַׁב הָאֶחָד עַל הַפֶּתַח וְלֹא מִלְּאָהוּ,
chunks.en: If the first one sat in the doorway and did not fill it,
chunks.st: one person sat in the entrance of a courtyard in which there is a deer, but did not fill the entire doorway,

chunks.en: and the second one sat and filled it,
chunks.st: and a second person sat and filled it,

chunks.en: the second one is chayav.
chunks.st: the second person is liable
chunks.stMore: because he completed the labor of trapping. However, if

chunks.en: If the first one sat in the doorway and filled it,
chunks.st: the first person sat in the doorway and filled it,

chunks.en: and the second one came and sat next to him,
chunks.st: and a second person came and sat next to him,

chunks.he: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁעָמַד הָרִאשׁוֹן וְהָלַךְ לוֹ,
chunks.en: even though the first one got up and went away,
chunks.st: the first person is liable and the second is exempt even if the first person stood and went

chunks.en: the first one is chayav and the second one is patur.
chunks.st: away, leaving the second one to secure the deer. The mishna explains:

chunks.en: What is this like?
chunks.st: To what is this second person’s action similar?

chunks.en: To someone who locks his house to guard it,
chunks.st: To one who locks his house to secure it,

chunks.en: and it turns out that a deer is guarded inside it.
chunks.st: and it turns out a deer that was trapped before Shabbat is also secured inside it.
chunks.stMore: In that case, he is exempt even though he enhances security on the deer, because he did not trap the animal.
